text:
Connor McDavid has a point in all 23 games Edmonton has played, 13 goals and 42 assists, and the streak has gone on so long that it has stopped being news and become the weather. He is producing 6.1 points per 60 minutes against a league rate of 2.1 for forwards.

Some of it will cool. He's shooting 20% (16% last season), and the Oilers have scored 27.5 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Finishing and on-ice luck drift back toward normal; that's not a knock, just arithmetic. What doesn't drift is how he moves the puck. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying it in on 68% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey rated him the most valuable forward in the league at 4.4 wins above replacement.

The new wrinkle is on the lineup card: Mike Babcock has split him from Leon Draisaitl, and Daily Faceoff's Oilersnation was asking whether that was the right call after a 5-2 win over Florida. Our range for his season runs from 147 to 181 points, which tells you how high the floor is even after the shooting comes down.
headline: McDavid has a point in every game
